seoTitle: How to Remove Buy and Sell Arrows in TradingView Charts
metaDescription: Buy and sell arrows cluttering your TradingView charts? Turn them off in the Trading settings tab to get a cleaner view for technical analysis.
intro: Those small up and down arrows marking past trade executions can clutter a TradingView chart, especially once you've got several trades logged and the labels start overlapping your candles. This guide shows exactly what those markers look like on a live chart and walks through the settings menu that controls them, so you can switch to a cleaner view for technical analysis without losing your actual trade history. It takes just a couple of clicks once you know which menu to open.

steps.heading: Spot the execution arrows on your chart
steps.body: On a BTCUSD chart with trade history, you'll see small blue chevron-style arrows sitting near recent price action, sometimes paired with quantity labels like "7 @ 118122" and "7 @ 118297" marking the price and size of each executed order. These render directly on top of your candles and moving averages, which is exactly why they start to feel like clutter once several show up close together on the same timeframe.

image.caption: A BTCUSD chart with an execution arrow rendered near the most recent candles, next to the live watchlist panel.

steps.heading: See how labels stack up over time
steps.body: On a daily chart covering a longer trade history, both a down arrow and an up arrow appear together with their price and quantity labels layered above the candles. The more trades you log, the more these accumulate, and on a shorter timeframe or a smaller chart window they can start to overlap the price action you're actually trying to read.

image.caption: Execution arrows and their quantity labels stacked above recent candles on a daily BTCUSD chart, showing how they accumulate with more trade history.

steps.heading: Open your chart settings
steps.body: With your chart open, click the settings gear or the "..." menu near the chart's symbol name at the top-left to bring up the display preferences window. This is the same settings panel that controls indicators, gridlines, and other visual elements on the chart, so it's worth knowing for other cleanup tasks too.

steps.heading: Go to the Trading tab
steps.body: Inside the settings window, find the tab related to trading or order execution — its exact label can shift slightly between TradingView updates, but it's generally grouped with other order-visibility options rather than under general chart appearance settings.

steps.heading: Uncheck executions and execution labels
steps.body: Scroll to the executions section and uncheck both the Executions and Execution labels boxes. These are checked by default, which is why the arrows and their price/quantity text show up automatically once you have trade history on that symbol — unchecking them controls the visual markers only, not your actual order data.

steps.heading: Confirm the change
steps.body: Click OK to save the settings, and the buy and sell arrows should disappear from your chart immediately, leaving just your candles and any indicators you've added. Your trade history itself is untouched — this setting only affects whether it renders visually on the chart.

faq.question: Where do I find the option to remove buy and sell arrows on TradingView?
faq.answer: It's inside the chart settings window, under the Trading tab, where you'll find the Executions and Execution labels checkboxes.

faq.question: Will removing the arrows delete my trade history?
faq.answer: No, unchecking Executions only hides the visual markers on the chart - it doesn't affect your actual trade records or account history.

faq.question: Does this work on TradingView mobile as well as desktop?
faq.answer: The settings menu is structured a bit differently on mobile, but a similar executions toggle is available to hide the arrows there too.

faq.question: Can I turn the arrows back on later if I change my mind?
faq.answer: Yes, just revisit the same Trading tab in chart settings and recheck the Executions and Execution labels boxes to bring them back.
